About

Energy engineering, data and making things

I'm in the final year of a B.Sc. in Energy Technology at LUT University, and I like problems where engineering, data and code meet.

I'm from Bangladesh, where I finished school at Dhaka College. I then studied software engineering for a semester at Universiti Malaya in Malaysia, and then came to Finland for energy engineering. That path shows in my work: I model energy systems, but I write my own code to do it.

My thesis brings the two together. I forecast electricity demand in the European steel industry and compare statistical and AI models, because better forecasts make it easier to run industry on wind and solar power.

I also like work I can hold and test: SolidWorks models that become 3D-printed prototypes, lab measurements and circuit simulations. At LUT I've worked as a tutor, helping new international students settle into university life.

Projects

Coursework, thesis and code, 2024–2026

Bachelor's thesis · in progress · 2026

AI-based energy demand forecasting to support renewable integration in the European iron and steel industry

Steel is one of Europe's most electricity-intensive industries, and better demand forecasts make it easier to plan around variable wind and solar supply. I run forecasting models on real European data and compare traditional statistical methods with AI-based methods.

Energy Systems · team of 5 · 2025

Microgrid design in HOMER Pro

Modelled a microgrid for a medium office in Houghton, USA: solar irradiance and load data, grid tariffs, then six energy sources (PV, a Tesla Powerpack battery, two generators, a converter and the grid) sized and compared on net present cost over 20 years at an 8% discount rate.

Energy technology laboratory

Eight lab works and three reports: temperature and pressure sensor calibration, air flow with an orifice plate and Pitot tube, electric motor efficiency, air heat pump COP, gamma radiation absorption and reservoir level measurement.

Wind & Solar Power · solo · 2026

Onshore wind farm design in Kymenlaakso

Chose a site near Summa using grid-connection data, analysed the Weibull wind distribution, estimated wake losses with the Jensen/WAsP model and calculated annual energy production for 5.5 MW turbines.

Weibull analysisWAsP wake modelAEPExcel
Energy Conversion Processes · individual · 2025

Waste heat recovery with an organic Rankine cycle

Designed an ORC with cyclohexane as the working fluid: evaporation at 250 °C with 10 K superheat, condensing at 40 °C, with a recuperator. Plotted the cycle on the log p–h diagram and calculated the power output and efficiency.

Smart EV charging station as a cyber-physical system

Python simulation of 14 chargers sharing a 120 kW grid connection. EVs arrive in morning and evening peaks, an allocation algorithm keeps total power under the limit, and a regression model predicts the daily peak demand.

Python simulations of cyber-physical systems

RLC circuit simulation in Simulink

Measurement & Control · team of 5 · 2025

DC motor speed control

Modelled a DC motor as a transfer function in MATLAB, checked open-loop phase margin and steady-state error, then designed a PI controller reaching a 72.4° phase margin, above the required 45°, with under 1% steady-state error.

Mechanical

Engineering Design · my part of a 4-person project · 2026

Car scissor jack: from calculation to printed prototype

Each of us designed one mechanism; the scissor jack was mine. I calculated the lifting mechanism, modelled its 10 components in SolidWorks, animated the assembly and 3D-printed the parts on a Prusa MK4S, my first print. The printed nut's thread wasn't accurate enough to run smoothly, so I corrected it by post-processing until the jack worked.

SolidWorksmotion studyPrusaSlicerPLAmechanism design
3D Modelling · team of 3 · 2026

Industrial mixing homogenizer

Our team of three designed an industrial mixing homogenizer. I modelled the complete mixing unit (rod, propeller, inlet and outlet rotors, screw and nut) with materials, tolerances and drawings, and put together the full machine assembly in SolidWorks. Teammates drew the frame, motor arm and wheels and produced the final assembly drawing sheet.
